Article text:
'Attention mechanisms have become a cornerstone of modern neural network architectures. Originally introduced to improve machine translation, attention allows a model to weigh the relevance of different parts of the input when producing each output. The key idea is to compute a set of attention weights that determine how much focus to place on each input element. These weights are typically learned during training. In practice, attention has been extended to self-attention, where the input attends to itself, enabling models to capture long-range dependencies. Despite its success, attention has limitations, including quadratic computational cost with respect to sequence length and potential overfitting on small datasets. Recent work has explored sparse and linearized attention variants to address these issues.'"
